correctness.rationale: For complete multipartite r>=3, a dominating set with support one must take an entire part; with >=2 supported parts it automatically dominates. For any selected vertex in V_i, outside neighbors consist of all omitted vertices outside that part, count B_S+sum_{h in S\{i}}y_h. Hence the inequalities are necessary and sufficient for every selected set; binomial choices of omissions yield exactly the claimed full cardinality polynomial. With K=k-B_S and total omissions Y, feasibility requires y_i>=max(0,Y-K) with caps n_i-1; the three upper bounds on Y by sum caps, K+min cap, and floor(sK/(s-1)) are also sufficient by an integer interval allocation argument. Thus minimum size at fixed support equals N-B_S-Y_S. Independent direct adjacency/neighbor checks agreed with support formula on 2920 graph-subset instances. Universal conclusion follows the counting/allocation proof.

The fixed-support minimum is a derived useful secondary formula; **the scalar global optimum itself is prior-covered and not credited as new**.
